intent: Approve a commit without a change check when only wording changed.

edit.summary:
I proposed four changes in the `authoring` domain. The draft check parses and reports no issues. I didn't touch `delivery`.

- **`objects.Commit`:** I added an optional boolean property `wording_only`.
- **`actions.approve_commit`:** The `checks-pass` precondition is now `checks_passed == true or wording_only == true`, and its reason text says so. It is still a person-only action, and `not-approved` is unchanged.
- **`actions.record_approval`:** The `approved-only-if-checked` precondition now also accepts `wording_only == true`. Without this, the kernel's approval record would still be refused.
- **`invariants.approved-commits-passed-their-checks`:** The check now also accepts `wording_only == true`. I changed it so a wording-only approval doesn't violate the invariant.

Nothing in the request or the declaration sets `wording_only` on a commit. I didn't add a way to set it, so you'll need to decide who or what sets it, such as the kernel when the commit is recorded or the owner.

This is a loosening of the check-before-approval rule. The change check will review it before it is deployed.

findings.problem: No action ever sets Commit.wording_only. record_check sets only checks_passed and failing, and no fixture has the field. The new `or target.wording_only == true` branches in the approve_commit precondition, the record_approval precondition and the invariant therefore never fire. If something outside the declaration does set it, nothing checks that only wording changed, so any commit could skip the change check on that flag alone.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: Commit.wording_only; actions approve_commit (checks-pass), record_approval (approved-only-if-checked); invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks

findings.problem: The change request says a commit may be approved without a change check when only wording changed. The purpose announcement still promises 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed.' The glossary 'change check' ('The checks a commit runs before approval') and 'approval' also still describe an unconditional check. The check_commit and cite_evidence reasons assume the same. These now contradict the new bypass.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: purpose.announcement; glossary (change check, approval)

findings.problem: The diff turns these elements to status 'proposed' and drops the owner's quote. The post-change files show them as 'confirmed', citing interview line L36 with no quote. Weakened safety rules are marked confirmed without a person's recorded words. The precondition checks-pass and the invariant keep their old quote or cite an unquoted line, and the old quote ('전부 다 추천한 거 동의', '19: a') agreed to the unconditional rule, not the new exception. Declared status and diff disagree.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: Commit object, approve_commit and its checks-pass precondition, record_approval, invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks

findings.problem: The existing scenario 'approve-only-after-a-passing-check' and the world fixtures cover only the checks_passed path. No scenario or fixture covers a wording_only commit with a failed or unrun check being approved, or wording_only combined with checks_passed false. The new behaviour is untested.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: scenarios, world.fixtures (Commit C1-C3)

findings.problem: Before, an approved commit always had a passing recorded check. Now an approved commit may have checks_passed false (for example C2 with wording_only set) and still be delivered. Delivery's description and the 'deliver' precondition ('Only an approved commit is delivered') rest on approval implying a passed check. The deploy floor does not recheck the change check, so the weakened guarantee carries through to deployment.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: deliver precondition 'approved'; delivery.domain.yaml: purpose.announcement ('Nothing that fails its checks ... gets there')

findings.problem: Nothing can ever set Commit.wording_only. record_commit, record_check and cite_evidence have no param or effect for it, and no kernel step is declared that works out whether only wording changed. The new exception is dead in practice. If a caller can set the flag itself, it lets any commit skip the change check on its own say-so, because nothing verifies that the diff really is wording only.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: Commit.wording_only; approve_commit precondition checks-pass; record_commit

findings.problem: The invariant, the approve_commit precondition and the record_approval precondition now accept an approval with no passing check.
